A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BSFA research and provide readable text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C. Matching content across pagination changes supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimization and training experiments, block ablations, memory measurements, and estimator timing results in Sections 3–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the training comparisons, ablations, and memory/runtime measurements in Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The BSFA update rule, Lanczos/PCA/block-wise estimators in Algorithms 1–4, and 4-bit variant are unchanged. The added related-work discussion introduces no procedural modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SST-2, CIFAR-10/100, ImageNet-1k, WikiText-103, and OpenWebText coverage, including the appendix timing evaluations. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The SGD/SGDM and AdamW/AdamMini comparator sets remain unchanged in corresponding experiments. Newly discussed IRE and Blockwise LR appear only in related work and are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Sections 3–5 and Appendix A retain the same model configurations, preprocessing, metrics, batch sizes, learning-rate schedules, training budgets, and tuning grids.

E4.justification: Both retain the same subspace-scaling experiments, PPE–LPE alignment analysis, block ablations, micro-batch memory comparison, 4-bit analysis, and appendix tuning curves.

E5.justification: Figure 3 continues to report results for three random seeds. Run-count information and uncertainty displays are unchanged, with no added confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 1–9 retain the same plotted results, and Tables 1–5 retain their entries. For example, Table 4 reports identical 50k-step losses: 2.77 for AdamW, 2.49 for BSFA, and 2.54 for 4bit-BSFA.

T1.justification: The subspace definitions, Proposition 1, its restatement and proof in Appendix C, and the Lanczos derivation in Appendix B.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about stability, PCA/block-wise estimation, approximately 2× Transformer acceleration, and up to 4× CIFAR acceleration.

C2.justification: Interpretations of subspace roles, block contributions, and memory trade-offs are unchanged. The same limitations concerning GPU memory and equal dominant-subspace ranks across blocks remain.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time disclosures, quantization/storage specifications, and implementation-source references remain unchanged, including in Appendices A and B.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds IRE (Wang et al., 2024) and Blockwise LR (Wang et al., 2025), with corresponding bibliography entries. It distinguishes BSFA's Hessian-eigenvector approach from their diagonal Fisher/Gauss–Newton and block-level scaling approaches, providing a focused extension of research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 2 locally shortens the momentum description and expands the final comparison paragraph. The section organization and nearly all remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: Local reflow moves Table 2 from PDF page 7 to page 8 and shifts existing figures, tables, and algorithms within pages. Their designs, axes, legends, and captions remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the completeness and clarity of research positioning by acknowledging IRE and Blockwise LR and explaining their relationship to BSFA in Section 2. This is a limited, evidence-supported gain: the methods, experimental support, proofs, and limitations remain unchanged, and the layout shifts introduce no material loss of readability.
